title: Manuel Perez, Buddy Bolden and the country bands' rivalry with the city
summary: Asked about Perez and Bolden, he did not see them play but says city people ranked his band the best.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What about people like Freddy Keppert and Manuel Perez and Buddy Bolden and Joe Alton? Did you hear those guys?
Well, I didn't get to see him. I didn't get to see him on the parade, Manuel.
You didn't see him, Manuel Perez? Yeah, Manuel.
Okay, let's see. You said you were talking about Manuel Perez, huh?

I think he's him. He got burned out. Anyway, we're going to the hospital and all. He's once, but I think he's him. It's been so long. Oh, for them guys to play hard, you know, you see. But the people in the city said we're the best band. They all give it to us. Yeah, see them, them men, they eat cornbread, see. You know, eat sanders like your city rats. Oh, they give it to us. We used to have two line-outs on each side, on each band. They have a line. They have a line out too. I know Clayborne and Williams, they had a band, all them guys. They had a band.
